Complete manifests, current PAS/ASH space cards, PAS letter rules, passgate screenplay scene setup/basis and relevant ASH screenplay authorization/capacity/actual-action passages checked. limitations: Concept-only review; no native grid, scaled collision, accessible route, engineering, hydraulic, clinical or runtime validation.
No characters or children appear in any of these eight review images; empty furniture does not establish vacancy, death, departure, refusal or consent.
Props do not establish potability, actual inventory, completed payment, staffed care, information-sharing authority or actual delivery.

findings.finding: Exactly two narrow beds with two individual blank wall tokens and separate personal bundles are visible in the civilian lodging room. Cushioned chairs in the care eave are seats, not extra beds; no people or children appear. Two separate cup cabinets distinguish military and civilian props. Both spaces open to ordinary foreground road without passing the rear military gate. However, distinct clean-supply and patient circulation is only suggested by lateral openings around the common front; final routing, separation and accessible thresholds need scaled design. No names or patient histories are displayed. Empty furniture establishes neither free capacity nor patient departure; one body occupies one actual bed, never separate military/civilian copies. Research consent remains separate from ordinary care.

Two mutually visible measuring bins under one roof have visibly different grain fill, and shelf gaps support finite supply. The wage counter has a closed cabinet, separate rectangular tokens, limited coin stacks and a worked-stone sample; a separate future-shift board remains blank. Horse/cart occupies the side unloading lane while foreground pedestrian approach remains outside the scales. No payment, actual escrow availability, renewed labor agreement or finished road is established. Exact capacity, quantities and pedestrian/cart clearance remain unverified.

Unmanned fixed load-sample bed is rope-separated from the foreground public bypass; a visibly unfinished rear segment is distinct. The right room has two separate closed cabinets, two keys and two closed purpose-ledgers with matching small marks, without exposing written personal records. Side door opens to civilian lane. Central single-person token is rendered as a small CLOSED-FOLIO-LIKE object with a mark, which risks reading as a third roster: replace with unmistakable single bed/person tally in production. Matching symbols are not proof of same patient or authorization to combine military, care, research and kinship data. Roof omission and test arrangement are conceptual, not load certification or collision evidence.

Exactly one sealed folded letter appears in the separate alcove, with no readable address or message and no duplicated original. Blank stay/leave token and tied-slats expiry-like prop occupy separate trays. Sparse grain and equipment/medicine shelves have empty bays and independent street access. Grain/medicine tokens became sample goods, and the shelf includes a small red-cross-like medical-box mark that should be reviewed or replaced with neutral period-appropriate art. Letter seal does not authorize reading or transmission; delivery must remove the original, and only an explicitly authorized copy may remain. The scene depicts neither completed delivery, family reply, agreed return date nor release/renewal of a job.

overall: Two civilian beds, purpose-separated records and one sealed original letter support finite capacity/privacy concepts. 113 single-person token resembles an extra folio; 114 prop/symbol refinements required. Independent civilian routes remain conceptual.
